books.title: Short Stories by Jesus
books.subtitle: The Enigmatic Parables of a Controversial Rabbi
books.author: Amy-Jill Levine
books.summary: Levine, a Jewish New Testament scholar, reads the parables in their first-century Jewish setting rather than through later Christian allegory.

books.title: The Misunderstood Jew
books.subtitle: The Church and the Scandal of the Jewish Jesus
books.author: Amy-Jill Levine
books.summary: Argues that Christian readings of Jesus often distort the Judaism he lived in, and corrects common misconceptions about first-century Jewish life.

books.title: Luke
books.subtitle: New International Biblical Commentary
books.author: Craig A. Evans
books.summary: A verse-by-verse commentary on the Gospel of Luke for general readers and students.

books.title: Narratives of a Vulnerable God
books.subtitle: Christ, Theology, and Scripture
books.author: William C. Placher
books.summary: A theological study of how the Gospel narratives portray Christ and what that implies for how Christians understand God.

books.title: The Power of Parable
books.subtitle: How Fiction by Jesus Became Fiction about Jesus
books.author: John Dominic Crossan
books.summary: Examines the parables as fiction told by Jesus and traces how the Gospel writers then turned them into fiction about him.

books.title: Jesus
books.subtitle: A Revolutionary Biography
books.author: John Dominic Crossan
books.summary: A historical reconstruction of Jesus's life and teaching, drawing on social-scientific study of first-century Mediterranean society.

books.title: Jesus the Jew
books.subtitle: A Historian's Reading of the Gospels
books.author: Geza Vermes
books.summary: Places Jesus within the charismatic Judaism of first-century Galilee, reading the Gospels as a historian of Judaism.

books.title: Jesus
books.subtitle: Apocalyptic Prophet of the New Millennium
books.author: Bart D. Ehrman
books.summary: Presents Jesus as a Jewish apocalyptic preacher who expected God to intervene in history within his own generation.

books.title: Meeting Jesus Again for the First Time
books.subtitle: The Historical Jesus and the Heart of Contemporary Faith
books.author: Marcus J. Borg
books.summary: Contrasts the historical Jesus with the Jesus of traditional Christian belief and explores what that distinction means for faith today.

books.title: The Righteous Mind
books.subtitle: Why Good People Are Divided by Politics and Religion
books.author: Jonathan Haidt
books.summary: Argues that moral judgments come mainly from fast intuition, with reasoning mostly justifying them afterward, and uses moral psychology to explain why people divide over politics and religion.

books.title: The Origins of Totalitarianism
books.author: Hannah Arendt
books.summary: Traces how antisemitism, imperialism, and the decline of the nation-state prepared the ground for Nazi and Stalinist rule.

books.title: The Shock Doctrine
books.subtitle: The Rise of Disaster Capitalism
books.author: Naomi Klein
books.summary: Contends that free-market reforms have repeatedly been pushed through in the aftermath of wars, coups, and disasters, while the public is disoriented.

books.title: The Great Fear
books.subtitle: The Anti-Communist Purge Under Truman and Eisenhower
books.author: David Caute
books.summary: A detailed history of the postwar campaign against suspected Communists: loyalty programs, congressional investigations, trials, and blacklists.

books.title: The Limits of Power
books.subtitle: The End of American Exceptionalism
books.author: Andrew J. Bacevich
books.summary: Argues that American overreach and political dysfunction have outrun the country's means, and that a more restrained foreign policy is needed.

books.title: What's the Matter with Kansas?
books.subtitle: How Conservatives Won the Heart of America
books.author: Thomas Frank
books.summary: Examines why many working-class Kansans vote Republican against their economic interests, arguing that cultural grievance has displaced economic politics.

books.title: The System
books.subtitle: Who Rigged It, How We Fix It
books.author: Robert B. Reich
books.summary: Contends that concentrated corporate wealth has captured American politics and rewritten economic rules in its favor, and proposes reforms.
